experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, known for its dramatic golden limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear turquoise waters. Hike the clifftop trail from Benagil and descend to the secluded cove for a refreshing swim.

experiences.name: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour
experiences.description: Paddle through the iconic Benagil Cave, one of the world's most beautiful sea caves, accessible only by water. A guided kayak tour takes you through hidden grottos and arches along the stunning Algarve coastline.

experiences.name: Algarve Wine & Vineyard Tour
experiences.description: Visit local Algarve wineries such as Quinta dos Vales or Adega do Cantor, sampling regional varieties including Negra Mole and Arinto. Enjoy guided cellar tours, vineyard walks, and paired tastings of local cheeses and charcuterie.

experiences.name: Ria Formosa Natural Park Boat Tour
experiences.description: Cruise through the Ria Formosa lagoon system, a protected natural park with barrier islands, salt marshes, and diverse birdlife. Stop at Ilha Deserta for a pristine unspoiled beach experience and fresh seafood lunch at the island's only restaurant.

experiences.name: Silves Medieval Castle & Old Town Food Walk
experiences.description: Explore the Moorish red sandstone castle of Silves, the ancient Algarve capital, then wander the cobblestone streets sampling local specialties including cataplana de marisco, almond pastries, and medronho brandy at traditional tascas.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Portugal Algarve
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Arrival day
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - Arrival day
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Faro Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Take the affordable Aerobus or shared shuttle to your accommodation at Aegean Bliss Resort in the Algarve beachfront area. Check in, freshen up, and get oriented with the resort surroundings.

meals.breakfast: N/A
meals.lunch: N/A
meals.dinner: Grab a quick late-night snack at a 24-hour convenience store or petrol station near the airport, or order a simple pizza/sandwich from a nearby late-night takeaway (~€5-8).

day_by_day.notes: Keep luggage light for easy transport. Pre-book a shared shuttle from Faro Airport to save money (approx €10-15 per person vs €40+ for a taxi). Have some euros in cash ready upon arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a leisurely wake-up, take a relaxed stroll along the beachfront promenade directly accessible from Aegean Bliss Resort. Explore the immediate shoreline, dip your toes in the Atlantic, and get your bearings in the local area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearest local beach (likely Meia Praia or a similar Algarve stretch depending on resort location). Spend the afternoon swimming, sunbathing, and enjoying the warm September sea. September is an ideal beach month with fewer crowds and warm water temperatures (~22°C).
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the local town waterfront or marina. Browse the evening passeio (evening stroll) culture of the Algarve. Find a local tasca (small traditional restaurant) for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy breakfast at the resort if included, or visit a local padaria (bakery) for a pastel de nata (custard tart) and galão (milky coffee) for ~€2-3.
meals.lunch: Pack snacks from a local supermarket (Lidl or Pingo Doce) for the beach — bread, local cheese, fruit, and water for ~€4-6.
meals.dinner: Find a local tasca serving prato do dia (dish of the day) — typically grilled fish, rice, and salad for ~€8-12. Ask locals for recommendations to avoid tourist-trap restaurants.

day_by_day.notes: September in the Algarve is warm and sunny (avg 25-28°C) with very little rain — perfect beach weather. Buy a reusable water bottle and fill up to save money throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local bus (EVA or Vamus Algarve network, ~€2-4) to Lagos, one of the Algarve's most stunning coastal towns. Explore the historic old town, walk the ancient city walls, and visit the Igreja de Santo António (free or minimal entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down to Praia Dona Ana and Praia do Camilo — two of the most photographed beaches in the Algarve with dramatic golden limestone cliffs. Swim, snorkel, or simply admire the scenery. Walk the clifftop path for spectacular views.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Lagos town center in the early evening. Browse the artisan market stalls and street performers around Praça Gil Eanes. Enjoy dinner in Lagos before taking the bus back to your resort.

meals.breakfast: Local café near bus station — toast with butter and jam plus espresso for ~€2-3.
meals.lunch: Pick up a bifana (pork sandwich) or freshly grilled sardine wrap from a beach kiosk or local snack bar near the cliffs for ~€4-6.
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Camões or similar local Lagos eatery — grilled sea bass (robalo) with potatoes and vegetables for ~€10-14. Share a carafe of house wine (~€4-5).

day_by_day.notes: Lagos is easily accessible by bus from most Algarve resorts. Buy a return ticket to save slightly. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the clifftop paths. Bring sunscreen and a hat.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Ponta da Piedade, the iconic sea cave and rock formation near Lagos (if not visited yesterday). Hire a local kayak (~€15-20 for 2 hours) or join a budget boat tour (~€15-20 per person) to explore the sea grottos and arches up close.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to your resort area and spend a relaxed afternoon at the resort beach. Try a different section of the local coastline if accessible on foot. Look for quieter coves away from the main tourist spots.
day_by_day.evening: Cook a simple meal at the resort (if kitchen facilities available) using fresh produce from a local market — grilled sardines, salad, and local bread. Alternatively, enjoy a sundowner at a beach bar and watch the famous Algarve sunset.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast or local café — scrambled eggs on toast and fresh orange juice for ~€4-5.
meals.lunch: Local supermarket picnic on the beach — local olives, presunto (cured ham), queijo da serra (local cheese), crusty bread, and a cold beer for ~€6-8.
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner at resort with market-fresh ingredients (~€8-10 for two) OR a beach bar meal of grilled chicken and fries for ~€9-12.

day_by_day.notes: Book kayak or boat tours directly at the dock to avoid online booking fees. Early morning kayaking (before 10am) offers calmer waters and fewer crowds. September light is golden and perfect for photography.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Sagres — the southwestern tip of Portugal and one of Europe's most dramatic coastal landscapes. Take the bus from Lagos or your nearest town (~€4-6 return). Visit Fortaleza de Sagres (fortress entry ~€3) and walk the dramatic clifftops above the Atlantic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Cabo de São Vicente (Cape St. Vincent) — the most southwesterly point of mainland Europe. The lighthouse and sheer 60-meter cliffs are breathtaking. Walk between Sagres and the Cape (about 6km round trip) or take a local taxi (~€5-8 one way).
day_by_day.evening: Return to your resort by early evening. Enjoy a quiet dinner at a local restaurant near the resort, reflecting on the dramatic landscapes of the day.

meals.breakfast: Early start — grab a pastel de nata and coffee at the bus station café for ~€2.
meals.lunch: Sagres has several affordable restaurants near the fortress — try cataplana de marisco (seafood stew) or grilled tuna steak (atum grelhado) for ~€10-13.
meals.dinner: Local resort area restaurant — simple grilled chicken piri-piri with rice and salad for ~€9-11.

day_by_day.notes: Sagres can be windy even in September — bring a light jacket. The bus schedule from Lagos to Sagres is limited, so check times carefully. Sunset at Cabo de São Vicente is legendary if timing works out.

day_by_day.morning: Wine tasting day! Research and visit a local Algarve winery. The Algarve has four wine regions (Lagos, Portimão, Lagoa, and Tavira DOC). Visit Adega do Cantor (near Guia/Albufeira area) or Quinta dos Vales (near Estômbar) — both offer affordable tasting sessions (~€10-15 per person including tour).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the wine experience at a second winery or visit a local wine shop/adega in town for a more informal tasting. Many local adegas offer free tastings if you purchase a bottle. Pick up a bottle of local Algarve red or white wine as a souvenir (~€5-8).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area. Enjoy the bottle of local wine purchased during the day at a beach sunset spot. Find a local restaurant specializing in petiscos (Portuguese tapas) for a light, affordable dinner.

meals.breakfast: Resort or local café — full Portuguese breakfast with toast, cheese, ham, and coffee for ~€4-6.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the winery if offered, or pack a picnic to enjoy in the vineyard grounds (~€5-7 self-catered).
meals.dinner: Petiscos restaurant — order 4-5 small dishes to share: chouriço assado (grilled sausage), pataniscas de bacalhau (cod fritters), pica-pau (marinated pork), and local bread for ~€12-15 for two people.

day_by_day.notes: Call ahead or book winery visits online to confirm opening hours and tour availability. Some smaller quintas prefer advance notice. The Algarve wine region is less famous than Douro or Alentejo but produces excellent, affordable wines.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Silves — the ancient Moorish capital of the Algarve. Take the train (cheapest option, ~€3-5) or bus to this stunning hilltop town. Explore the magnificent red sandstone Castelo de Silves (entry ~€2.80) with panoramic views over the surrounding countryside.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through Silves old town, visit the Gothic Cathedral (free), and browse the local market if it's a market day. Explore the banks of the Rio Arade river below the castle. The area is surrounded by orange and fig orchards — a beautiful contrast to the coastal scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by early evening. Enjoy a relaxing evening swim at the resort beach as the September sun sets. Have dinner at a casual resort-area restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Train station café — coffee and tosta mista (toasted ham and cheese sandwich) for ~€2.50.
meals.lunch: Silves local restaurant near the castle — try medronho (local firewater) as an aperitif, then grilled pork with orange sauce (a regional specialty) for ~€10-12.
meals.dinner: Resort area casual restaurant — fresh grilled sea bream (dourada) with boiled potatoes and salad for ~€11-13.

day_by_day.notes: Silves is inland and slightly cooler than the coast — a welcome change. The train from Tunes station connects to Silves cheaply. The Silves Medieval Fair usually takes place in August, but the town is charming year-round. Try medronho liqueur — it's made from local strawberry trees.

day_by_day.morning: Beach day focused on water sports. Visit a local surf or water sports school near your resort. September has excellent conditions for beginner surfing lessons (~€25-35 including board and wetsuit) or stand-up paddleboarding (SUP) hire (~€10-15/hour).
day_by_day.afternoon: After water sports, relax on the beach. Walk along the shoreline to explore further stretches of coastline accessible from the resort. Look for sea caves or rock pools at low tide.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner drinks at a beachfront bar. Watch the famous Algarve golden hour. Then head to a local restaurant for a celebratory seafood dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early energizing breakfast — local café with scrambled eggs, toast, fresh orange juice, and coffee for ~€5-6.
meals.lunch: Beach kiosk or snack bar — toasted sandwich (tosta) and a cold Sagres beer for ~€5-7.
meals.dinner: Seafood restaurant — arroz de marisco (seafood rice) is a Portuguese classic and usually serves 2 people for ~€18-22 total. Share with a travel companion or order half portion.

day_by_day.notes: September surf conditions in the Algarve are generally mellow — ideal for beginners. Always check tide times before exploring rock pools. SPF 50 sunscreen is essential even in September.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip east to Tavira — arguably the most beautiful town in the Algarve. Take the train (~€4-8 depending on origin) to this elegant Moorish-influenced town. Walk across the Roman bridge, explore the castle ruins (free), and admire the distinctive four-sided chimneys unique to the eastern Algarve.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a short ferry or water taxi (~€1.50 each way) from Tavira to Ilha de Tavira — a stunning barrier island beach within the Ria Formosa Natural Park. The beach here is pristine and less commercialized than western Algarve beaches. Swim and relax.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tavira town for early evening. Browse the lively Praça da República before catching the train back. Have dinner in Tavira before departing.

meals.breakfast: Train journey breakfast — pack fruit and yogurt from the supermarket the night before (~€2-3).
meals.lunch: Beach kiosk on Ilha de Tavira — simple grilled fish sandwich and cold drink for ~€6-8.
meals.dinner: Tavira restaurant near the river — bacalhau à brás (scrambled eggs with shredded salt cod and crispy potatoes) — a Portuguese classic for ~€10-12.

day_by_day.notes: Tavira is in the eastern Algarve (Sotavento) and has a distinctly different, more traditional character than the western tourist areas. The Ria Formosa is a protected wetland — respect the natural environment. Last ferries back from the island are usually around 19:00-20:00 in September.

day_by_day.morning: Second wine tasting experience — visit a different winery or take a guided wine tour of the Lagoa wine region. Quinta da Penina or local Lagoa cooperative wineries offer affordable tours. The Lagoa DOC is known for its white wines. Tour and tasting typically ~€10-15.
day_by_day.afternoon: After wine tasting, visit the nearby town of Carvoeiro — a charming small resort town with a beautiful beach nestled between cliffs. Walk the Algar Seco boardwalk along the dramatic rock formations and sea caves (free, spectacular views).
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort. Enjoy a relaxed evening — perhaps buy a bottle of wine from today's tasting and enjoy it on the resort terrace or beach while watching the sunset.

meals.breakfast: Resort or local padaria — fresh bread rolls with local honey and butter, plus coffee for ~€3-4.
meals.lunch: Carvoeiro village — small local restaurant with daily fish specials for ~€9-12. The village has several affordable options away from the main tourist strip.
meals.dinner: Self-catered at resort — visit a local market for fresh produce: grilled sardines, salad, local bread, and a glass of today's wine purchase for ~€8-10 total.

day_by_day.notes: Carvoeiro is best visited on foot or by local bus. The Algar Seco rock formations are most dramatic at mid-morning when the light hits the ochre limestone. Wine cooperatives often sell bottles at cellar-door prices significantly cheaper than supermarkets.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Albufeira — the Algarve's most famous resort town. Explore the historic old town (zona velha) which retains genuine Portuguese character despite the tourism. Visit the fish market in the morning when it's most active. Browse local craft shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the tunnel walkway down to Praia dos Pescadores (Fishermen's Beach) in Albufeira old town — a beautiful beach framed by white-painted buildings. Spend the afternoon swimming and people-watching. Walk east along the clifftop path to discover quieter beaches.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy Albufeira's lively evening atmosphere in the old town. Browse the evening market and street performers. Have dinner at a local restaurant before returning to your resort.

meals.breakfast: Albufeira old town café — fresh pastries and galão coffee for ~€3-4.
meals.lunch: Waterfront snack bar near the beach — grilled chicken pitta with salad and a cold drink for ~€7-9.
meals.dinner: Old town restaurant — try açorda de gambas (shrimp bread soup) or grilled lulas (squid) with garlic and olive oil for ~€10-13. House wine carafe ~€4-5.

day_by_day.notes: Albufeira can be very touristy — stay in the old town area for the most authentic experience. Avoid the 'Strip' area which is oriented toward British package tourists. September means fewer crowds than July/August — much more pleasant.

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach day — return to your favorite beach discovered during the trip for a leisurely morning. Alternatively, explore any nearby beaches not yet visited. Rent a bicycle (~€10-15/day) to explore the local coastline at your own pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local mercado municipal (covered market) for fresh produce, local cheeses, smoked meats, and artisan goods. Stock up on affordable Portuguese souvenirs: local wine, medronho liqueur, flor de sal (Algarve sea salt), and carob products — all much cheaper at local markets than tourist shops.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner — splurge slightly on a nice seafood restaurant for a memorable last evening. Cataplana (traditional copper pot seafood stew) is the signature dish of the Algarve and worth trying for a special occasion. Enjoy a final glass of local wine watching the sunset.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — enjoy all amenities on your last full day.
meals.lunch: Market lunch — assemble a feast from market purchases: local cheeses, cured meats, olives, fresh bread, and fruit for ~€8-10.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a quality local restaurant — cataplana de marisco for two (~€25-30 shared) with a bottle of local Algarve white wine (~€10-12). Splurge night within budget!

day_by_day.notes: Buy vacuum-packed local products (cheeses, smoked sausages) at the market — they travel well and make excellent gifts. Flor de sal from the Algarve salt pans is a world-class product sold very cheaply locally. Book the farewell dinner restaurant in advance for September evenings.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — pack bags and check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Take one last walk on the beach to soak in the Algarve atmosphere. Grab breakfast at a local café and pick up any last-minute souvenirs from nearby shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time, either head directly to Faro Airport or spend a few hours in Faro city center. Faro old town (Cidade Velha) is worth a quick visit — the walled old town, cathedral, and bone chapel (Igreja dos Ossos) are all within walking distance of the bus/train station.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Faro Airport. Allow at least 2 hours before departure for check-in and security. Take the Aerobus or shared shuttle from your resort/Faro city center to the airport (~€10-15).

meals.breakfast: Local café — final pastel de nata and bica (espresso) for ~€2. A Portuguese farewell!
meals.lunch: Faro old town café or airport (budget for airport prices ~€10-15) — or pack snacks purchased at the local supermarket for the journey.
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight meal depending on departure time.

day_by_day.notes: Faro Airport is small and manageable — but September sees high traffic as summer season winds down. Arrive early. The Faro old town bone chapel (Capelo dos Ossos at Igreja do Carmo) charges ~€3 entry and is a fascinating, unique sight for a quick final morning visit. Keep €5-10 in euros for any final transport or snacks.

trip_options.title: Classic Portugal Algarve Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, known for its dramatic golden limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear turquoise waters. Hike the clifftop trail from Benagil and descend to the secluded cove for a refreshing swim.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Late arrival day
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - Late arrival day
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Faro Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort in the Algarve beachfront. Check in, freshen up, and unwind with a welcome drink at the hotel bar before heading to bed.

meals.breakfast: N/A
meals.lunch: N/A
meals.dinner: Light snack or late-night bite at the hotel bar upon arrival — try a Portuguese pastel de nata and a glass of local wine to settle in.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Pre-arrange airport transfer with the resort ahead of time to avoid stress. Pack a snack for the flight in case you arrive hungry. The hotel bar typically serves until midnight.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. After breakfast, take a relaxed orientation walk along the beachfront promenade directly in front of the Aegean Bliss Resort. Get your bearings, feel the Atlantic breeze, and dip your toes in the sea for the first time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon on the resort's beach or the adjacent public beach. Rent a sunbed and umbrella, swim in the calm September sea, and explore the nearby sea caves or rock formations on foot at low tide.
day_by_day.evening: Head into the nearest town center (Lagos or Albufeira depending on resort location) for a stroll through the old town. Browse local shops and settle into a traditional tasca for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Full buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — fresh fruit, local cheeses, eggs, and pastries.
meals.lunch: Casual beachside café near the resort — grilled sardine sandwich (bifana de sardinha) and a cold Sagres beer (~€10–14).
meals.dinner: O Camilo or a similar traditional restaurant in Lagos — try the cataplana de marisco (seafood stew) for two (~€25–35 per person).

day_by_day.notes: September in the Algarve is ideal — warm sea temperatures (~22°C), fewer crowds than peak summer, and golden light. Apply sunscreen even on cloudy days.

day_by_day.morning: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim — one of the Algarve's crown jewels. Drive or take a taxi (~20 min from most Algarve resort areas) to Praia da Marinha. Begin the dramatic clifftop trail along the Seven Hanging Valleys (Sete Vales Suspensos) section of the Rota Vicentina. Marvel at the golden limestone arches, sea stacks, and hidden grottos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend to Praia da Marinha beach itself via the wooden staircase. Swim in the crystal-clear turquoise water surrounded by towering cliffs. Snorkel around the rock formations and sea caves — bring your own gear or rent locally. Pack a picnic lunch to enjoy on the beach.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a shower and rest. Head to a nearby wine bar for an evening of Algarve wine tasting — try local Vinho Regional Algarve whites and reds from producers like Quinta dos Vales.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort.
meals.lunch: Packed picnic on Praia da Marinha — grab supplies from a local Pingo Doce supermarket the night before: local cheese, presunto (cured ham), olives, crusty bread, and fruit (~€8–10).
meals.dinner: Restaurante Sueste in Ferragudo or a wine-focused bistro nearby — grilled sea bass (robalo) with local white wine (~€22–30 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Start the Marinha hike early (by 9:00 AM) to beat the heat and secure a good spot on the beach. Wear sturdy shoes for the clifftop trail. The full Seven Valleys hike is approximately 11 km — you can do a shorter out-and-back version if preferred. Bring plenty of water.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Sagres and the dramatic Cabo de São Vicente — the southwesternmost point of continental Europe. Explore the 16th-century Fortaleza de Sagres fortress perched on the clifftops. Walk the windswept promontory and watch the Atlantic crash against the rocks far below.
day_by_day.afternoon: From Sagres, drive a few minutes to Praia do Beliche or Praia da Mareta — two of the most unspoiled beaches in the Algarve with wild, dramatic scenery. Swim and relax in the afternoon sun. Surfers often gather here — great for watching if you're not surfing yourself.
day_by_day.evening: Dine in Sagres village at a local restaurant. The town has a laid-back surf-town vibe with excellent fresh fish restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort.
meals.lunch: Snack bar near Praia da Mareta — fresh grilled fish of the day with salad and local bread (~€12–16).
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Telheiro do Infante in Sagres — famous for its fresh tuna and swordfish steaks (~€20–28 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Sagres is approximately 45–60 min drive from the central Algarve. Rent a car for this day if you haven't already — it gives you the most flexibility. The wind at Cabo de São Vicente can be surprisingly strong even in September; bring a light layer.

day_by_day.morning: Wine tasting morning at Quinta dos Vales — one of the Algarve's premier wine estates near Estômbar/Lagoa. Take a guided vineyard tour to learn about the unique Algarve terroir, grape varieties (Negra Mole, Síria, Arinto), and winemaking process. The estate also features impressive outdoor sculpture art.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the wine tour, visit the charming riverside town of Silves — the ancient Moorish capital of the Algarve. Explore the magnificent red sandstone Castelo de Silves, one of the best-preserved Moorish castles in Portugal. Wander the cobblestone streets and visit the Gothic cathedral.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner in Silves old town before returning to the resort.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort.
meals.lunch: Wine and cheese pairing lunch included with the Quinta dos Vales wine tour, or a light tapas lunch in a nearby café (~€15–20 with wine).
meals.dinner: Café Inglês in Silves — a beloved local institution with Portuguese cuisine in a historic setting (~€18–25 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Book the Quinta dos Vales wine tour in advance — tours typically run at 10:00 AM and 3:00 PM. The tour costs approximately €15–25 per person and includes tastings of 4–6 wines. Purchase a bottle or two to enjoy back at the resort.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Praia de Benagil and the famous Benagil Sea Cave (Algar de Benagil) — one of Portugal's most iconic natural wonders. Take a kayak or stand-up paddleboard tour from Benagil beach to paddle into the cathedral-like cave with its stunning domed ceiling and interior beach. Book in advance as tours fill up quickly.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the cave tour, relax on Praia de Benagil or walk the clifftop path east toward Praia de Carvalho for a quieter beach experience. Swim in the incredibly clear water and explore small hidden grottoes along the cliff base.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for sunset drinks on the terrace. Enjoy a quiet evening at the hotel pool bar or resort restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort.
meals.lunch: Small beach café at Benagil — fresh grilled fish, salad, and a cold beer (~€14–18).
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant at Aegean Bliss — try the fresh catch of the day with a bottle of Algarve white wine. Treat yourself to a mid-range resort dinner (~€25–35 per person).

day_by_day.notes: The Benagil Cave kayak/SUP tour must be booked at least 2–3 days in advance in September. Tours depart early morning (8:00–10:00 AM) for the calmest sea conditions. You cannot enter the cave by swimming — a boat, kayak, or SUP is required. Several reputable operators offer tours from €25–35 per person.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the picturesque town of Lagos — one of the Algarve's most beautiful and historic towns. Explore the old town walls, the Slave Market Museum (Mercado de Escravos), and the Igreja de Santo António with its stunning gilded baroque interior. Stroll the cobblestone streets and browse local artisan shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short boat trip to the incredible rock formations and beaches around Ponta da Piedade — Lagos's signature sea stacks, arches, and grottos. A short boat tour from Lagos marina (~€15–20) is the best way to see the formations up close. Alternatively, hike the clifftop path for panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Lagos for dinner and evening drinks. The town has a vibrant but relaxed nightlife scene perfect for a mid-range traveler.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort.
meals.lunch: Tasca do Celso in Lagos — a beloved local lunch spot with daily specials, fresh fish, and house wine (~€12–18 per person).
meals.dinner: A Forja restaurant in Lagos — excellent traditional Portuguese cuisine, known for cataplana and fresh seafood (~€22–30 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Lagos is approximately 30–45 min from most Algarve resort areas. It's very walkable once you're in the old town. The Ponta da Piedade boat tours run throughout the day from Lagos marina — the late afternoon light makes for spectacular photography.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed beach morning at the resort. Sleep in, enjoy a long breakfast, and spend the morning on the beach reading, swimming, or simply soaking up the September sunshine. This is a deliberate rest day built into the itinerary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Optional: Take a beginner surf lesson at a local surf school near the resort (many operate along the Algarve coast, ~€35–45 for a 2-hour group lesson). Alternatively, rent a kayak or pedalo from the beach and explore the coastline at your own pace.
day_by_day.evening: Visit a local wine shop or adega (wine cellar) in the nearest town for a self-guided tasting of Alentejo and Algarve wines — the shop staff are usually very knowledgeable and happy to guide you through local producers.

meals.breakfast: Extended hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — take your time.
meals.lunch: Beachside chiringuito (beach bar) near the resort — grilled prawns, pataniscas de bacalhau (salt cod fritters), and a glass of chilled vinho verde (~€15–20).
meals.dinner: Local tasca in the nearby village — try arroz de lingueirão (razor clam rice) or amêijoas à bulhão pato (clams in garlic and coriander) (~€18–24 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Rest days are important on a 13-day trip. Don't feel obligated to fill every moment. September's warm evenings are perfect for slow, lingering dinners on a restaurant terrace.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Faro — the Algarve's elegant capital city. Explore the walled Cidade Velha (Old Town) with its Roman walls, the stunning Sé Cathedral (climb the tower for panoramic views), and the charming Largo da Sé square. Visit the hauntingly beautiful Bone Chapel (Igreja dos Ossos) at the Carmo Church.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a short ferry (€2.50 each way) from Faro harbor to the Ria Formosa Natural Park barrier islands — Ilha Deserta or Ilha da Culatra. These pristine, undeveloped islands have some of the most beautiful and uncrowded beaches in the Algarve. Swim, walk, and relax in near-total tranquility.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Faro for dinner in the old town before driving back to the resort.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort.
meals.lunch: Snack bar on Ilha Deserta or Ilha da Culatra — fresh grilled fish straight off the boats, with local salad (~€14–18).
meals.dinner: Restaurante Cidade Velha in Faro — excellent Portuguese cuisine in a historic setting within the old city walls (~€22–30 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Faro is 30–45 min from most Algarve resort areas. Check the ferry schedule from Faro harbor in advance — boats run regularly but less frequently in the late afternoon. The Ria Formosa islands are a UNESCO-recognized ecosystem and a genuine hidden gem.

day_by_day.morning: Wine and culinary experience: Join a guided Algarve food and wine tour or visit the Adega do Cantor winery (owned by Cliff Richard) near Guia/Albufeira, or Quinta da Tôr near Loulé. Tour the vineyards, learn about organic and biodynamic winemaking in the Algarve, and participate in a structured tasting of premium local wines.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the traditional market town of Loulé — the Algarve's largest inland market. The covered market (Mercado de Loulé) is a beautiful Moorish-inspired building filled with fresh produce, local cheeses, honey, almonds, carob, and Algarve specialties. Browse the artisan stalls and pick up local souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a sunset swim before dinner. Enjoy dinner at the resort or a nearby upscale restaurant as a mid-trip treat.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort.
meals.lunch: Market lunch at Loulé market — assemble your own spread from market stalls: local cheeses, olives, smoked meats, fresh bread, and fruit (~€10–15).
meals.dinner: Loulé Jardim or a quality restaurant near the resort — try the local specialty of figs with almonds and carob for dessert (~€25–35 per person with wine).

day_by_day.notes: Loulé market is most vibrant on Saturday mornings — if Day 10 falls on a Saturday, make the market the morning priority and adjust the winery visit accordingly. Book winery tours in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Golden Triangle area — visit Vilamoura marina, one of the most glamorous marinas in Europe. Walk the waterfront, admire the yachts, and visit the Roman ruins of Cerro da Vila right next to the marina (a surprisingly impressive archaeological site with mosaics and baths).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Praia de Vilamoura or Praia da Falésia — a stunning 6-km stretch of beach backed by dramatic red and orange cliffs. This is one of the longest and most beautiful beaches in the Algarve. Spend the afternoon swimming and relaxing on this spectacular stretch of coastline.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sundowner cruise from Vilamoura marina — several operators offer 2-hour sunset catamaran cruises with wine and canapés (~€35–50 per person). Watch the sun dip into the Atlantic from the water.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort.
meals.lunch: Café or restaurant on Praia da Falésia — grilled chicken piri-piri or fresh tuna salad (~€12–16).
meals.dinner: Restaurante Marlim in Vilamoura marina area — excellent fresh seafood with marina views (~€25–35 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Book the sunset catamaran cruise at least 2 days in advance — very popular in September. Wine and snacks are typically included. Bring a light jacket as it can get breezy on the water after sunset.

day_by_day.morning: Final beach morning — return to your favorite beach from the trip or discover a new one. Consider Praia do Camilo near Lagos (small, dramatic, accessed via steep wooden stairs through cliffs) or Praia de Odeceixe on the border of the Algarve and Alentejo for a wilder, more remote experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Souvenir shopping and last-minute exploration. Visit a local ceramics shop for hand-painted azulejo tiles, a deli for local products (medronho brandy, carob syrup, local olive oil, almond sweets), and a wine shop to stock up on Algarve bottles to take home.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner — splurge slightly on a special final meal. Choose a restaurant that best represents your favorite flavors of the trip.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort.
meals.lunch: Casual beach café — keep it light and fresh: grilled fish, salad, and a glass of local rosé (~€14–18).
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a top local restaurant — try a full cataplana feast (traditional copper pot seafood or meat stew) for two, with a bottle of premium Algarve red wine (~€35–45 per person). Toast to a wonderful trip.

day_by_day.notes: Pack your suitcase this evening and prepare for the final day. Keep receipts for any VAT refund claims on purchases over €50 at participating stores. Double-check your flight details for tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the Algarve. Enjoy a last leisurely breakfast at the resort. Take one final walk on the beach to breathe in the sea air and soak in the views of the Atlantic. Collect any remaining belongings and check out of the Aegean Bliss Resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, either head directly to Faro Airport (allow 45–60 min from most resort areas) or squeeze in a final coffee and pastel de nata at a local café in the nearest town. Browse the airport shops for any last-minute Portuguese wine or port to take home.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Faro Airport. Carry the memories of 13 incredible days in the Algarve — the golden cliffs, the turquoise sea, the sea caves, the wine, and the warmth of Portuguese hospitality.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — make it count.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a café near the resort or at Faro Airport — a simple sandwich (tosta mista) and coffee (~€5–8).
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant or in-flight meal depending on departure time.

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 11:00–12:00 noon. Confirm with the resort whether you can store luggage if your flight is in the late afternoon. Faro Airport is small and efficient — arrive 2 hours before departure. Obrigado e boa viagem — Thank you and safe travels!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Portugal Algarve Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, known for its dramatic golden limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear turquoise waters. Hike the clifftop trail from Benagil and descend to the secluded cove for a refreshing swim.

experiences.name: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour
experiences.description: Paddle through the iconic Benagil Cave, one of the world's most beautiful sea caves, accessible only by water. A guided kayak tour takes you through hidden grottos and arches along the stunning Algarve coastline.

experiences.name: Algarve Wine & Vineyard Tour
experiences.description: Visit local Algarve wineries such as Quinta dos Vales or Adega do Cantor, sampling regional varieties including Negra Mole and Arinto. Enjoy guided cellar tours, vineyard walks, and paired tastings of local cheeses and charcuterie.

experiences.name: Ria Formosa Natural Park Boat Tour
experiences.description: Cruise through the Ria Formosa lagoon system, a protected natural park with barrier islands, salt marshes, and diverse birdlife. Stop at Ilha Deserta for a pristine unspoiled beach experience and fresh seafood lunch at the island's only restaurant.

experiences.name: Silves Medieval Castle & Old Town Food Walk
experiences.description: Explore the Moorish red sandstone castle of Silves, the ancient Algarve capital, then wander the cobblestone streets sampling local specialties including cataplana de marisco, almond pastries, and medronho brandy at traditional tascas.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Faro Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. A private luxury transfer arranged by Aegean Bliss Resort will greet you at arrivals with a name board. Settle into your Beachfront suite, enjoy a welcome amenity (chilled Vinho Verde, local cheese board) prepared by the resort, and take a moment to unwind on your private terrace overlooking the Atlantic.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight
meals.lunch: N/A — in-flight
meals.dinner: Late-night welcome cheese & charcuterie board with Algarve wines in your suite, arranged by the resort concierge

day_by_day.notes: Request the concierge to confirm all upcoming experience bookings upon check-in. Ensure passports and travel documents are safely stored. Resort check-in is available 24/7 for late arrivals.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely resort breakfast followed by a private orientation walk along the beachfront promenade. Spend the late morning settling in — explore the resort's infinity pool, spa facilities, and beachfront cabanas. A gentle introduction to the Algarve's golden coast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim — join a small-group guided coastal hike along one of the Algarve's most dramatic stretches of golden limestone cliffs. Swim in the crystal-clear turquoise coves tucked between the rock formations. A premium guide provides geological and historical context. Towels, snorkeling gear, and chilled refreshments are included.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort's clifftop bar. Dine at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant with panoramic Atlantic views, indulging in a tasting menu featuring locally caught seafood and Algarve-inspired cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Full à la carte breakfast at the resort's oceanfront restaurant — fresh pastéis, local honey, acai bowls, eggs Benedict with smoked bacalhau
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic box prepared by the resort chef, enjoyed on the cliffs at Praia da Marinha — includes artisan bread, Iberian ham, local cheeses, fruit, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Resort signature restaurant — 6-course tasting menu with optional Algarve wine pairing; highlights include grilled tiger prawns, cataplana de marisco, and almond-based desserts

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable hiking shoes and reef-safe sunscreen for the coastal hike. September weather is warm (24–28°C) with calm seas — ideal for swimming in the coves.

day_by_day.morning: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour — depart early morning for the iconic Benagil Cave, one of the world's most photographed sea caves. Paddle through the cathedral-like interior where sunlight streams through the natural oculus onto the sandy floor below. A private luxury kayak tour ensures exclusivity, with a certified guide, top-of-the-range equipment, and a chilled refreshment pack.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a leisurely poolside lunch. Spend the afternoon at the resort's private beach, enjoying watersports offerings (paddleboarding, jet ski, or a private catamaran sunset cruise can be pre-booked). Alternatively, book a 90-minute couples' massage at the resort spa.
day_by_day.evening: Private dining experience on the beach — the resort can arrange a candlelit table directly on the sand with a personal chef preparing a bespoke seafood menu, accompanied by a curated wine selection.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the resort before departure — croissants, fresh juice, espresso, and seasonal fruit
meals.lunch: Poolside à la carte lunch at the resort — grilled sea bass, quinoa salad, fresh gazpacho, and craft cocktails
meals.dinner: Private beach dinner for two — lobster thermidor, seared tuna tataki, and a Douro Valley red wine pairing; arranged by resort concierge (advance booking required)

day_by_day.notes: The Benagil Cave kayak tour is best done at low tide in the morning for the most dramatic light. Confirm tidal schedules with the tour operator the evening before. Bring waterproof phone case.

day_by_day.morning: Algarve Wine & Vineyard Tour (Morning Session) — a private chauffeured tour departs the resort heading inland to the lush wine country. First stop: Quinta dos Vales, a prestigious estate known for its award-winning reds and whites. Enjoy a guided vineyard walk with the winemaker, learning about the unique terroir of the Algarve's limestone and clay soils.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the wine tour to Adega do Cantor (the winery associated with Sir Cliff Richard), set amid rolling hills with stunning countryside views. Enjoy a premium seated tasting of 5–6 wines paired with local charcuterie, regional cheeses, and artisan bread in a private tasting room.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort in the late afternoon. Freshen up and head out for dinner at a renowned local restaurant in Carvoeiro or Lagoa town — a charming whitewashed village setting with authentic Algarvian cuisine elevated to fine-dining standards.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — full Portuguese spread with fresh-pressed orange juice, smoked sausages, local jams, and pastéis de nata
meals.lunch: Wine-paired charcuterie and cheese tasting lunch at Adega do Cantor — included in the premium tour experience
meals.dinner: Restaurant recommendation: Bon Bon (Carvoeiro) — Michelin-starred, celebrated for creative tasting menus with local Algarve ingredients and exceptional wine list

day_by_day.notes: Pace wine tastings to enjoy the full afternoon tour. A private driver is essential — do not self-drive. Bon Bon restaurant requires advance reservation; book at least 2 weeks prior through the concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Ria Formosa Natural Park Boat Tour — depart by private luxury speedboat from a nearby marina heading east to the UNESCO-recognized Ria Formosa lagoon system. Glide through serene waterways, spot flamingos, herons, and migratory birds, and explore the pristine barrier islands with their untouched sandy beaches. A naturalist guide provides expert commentary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Disembark on one of the barrier islands (Ilha Deserta or Ilha de Tavira) for a private beach picnic. Swim in the calm, warm lagoon waters. Explore the salt marshes on foot before the boat returns to the marina in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a stylish rooftop bar in Faro's Old Town, followed by dinner at a premium restaurant in the historic city centre, exploring the rich cultural heritage of the Algarve's capital.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast — smoked salmon on sourdough, avocado, poached eggs, and fresh juice
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic on the barrier island — prepared by the resort: smoked octopus salad, artisan sandwiches, tropical fruit, chilled rosé wine
meals.dinner: Restaurant recommendation: Faz Gostos (Faro) — intimate fine-dining in a historic mansion, celebrated for modern Portuguese cuisine and exceptional regional wine cellar

day_by_day.notes: Bring biodegradable sunscreen to protect the sensitive Ria Formosa ecosystem. The lagoon waters are calm and warm in September — ideal for a relaxing swim. Faro Old Town is walkable from most parking areas.

day_by_day.morning: Silves Medieval Castle & Old Town Food Walk — a private chauffeured excursion to Silves, the ancient Moorish capital of the Algarve. Begin with a guided tour of the magnificent red sandstone castle, exploring its towers, battlements, and cisterns with a specialist historian guide. Enjoy panoramic views over the orange groves and cork forests of the Algarve interior.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a curated food walk through Silves' cobblestone streets — sample local specialties including folar (regional bread), amêijoas na cataplana (clam stew), almond sweets, medronho (arbutus berry spirit), and artisan olive oils. Visit the weekly local market (if timing aligns) for fresh produce and crafts.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by late afternoon. Enjoy a relaxing evening — optional resort spa treatment (hot stone massage or vinotherapy facial). Dinner at the resort's informal beach grill for a more relaxed but still premium experience.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — full à la carte spread
meals.lunch: Food walk tastings in Silves serve as a progressive lunch — multiple stops featuring regional specialties; supplemented by a sit-down meal at Marisqueira Rui (Silves), a legendary seafood restaurant
meals.dinner: Resort beach grill — wood-fired whole fish, grilled Algarve prawns, charred vegetables, and a bottle of Alentejo white wine under the stars

day_by_day.notes: Silves is approximately 45 minutes from the resort by private car. The castle is open from 09:00; arriving early avoids weekend crowds. September is harvest season — orange groves and vineyards are at their most picturesque.

day_by_day.morning: Full resort day — a true luxury rest day. Begin with a sunrise yoga session on the beach (arranged by the resort wellness team). Then enjoy a long, indulgent breakfast before a private 90-minute deep tissue or Ayurvedic massage at the resort spa.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the resort's full facilities — infinity pool, hydrotherapy pool, private beach. Alternatively, arrange a private sailing charter departing from the nearby marina for a 3-hour afternoon sail along the Algarve coast, with champagne and canapés on deck.
day_by_day.evening: Dress for a special evening — arrange a private helicopter sunset flight over the Algarve coastline (bookable through the concierge), followed by a celebratory dinner at the resort's fine-dining restaurant with a premium Champagne toast.

meals.breakfast: Extended luxury breakfast — live cooking station, smoked fish selection, pastry trolley, Champagne mimosas
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch — sushi platter, ceviche, chilled lobster bisque, and fresh watermelon juice
meals.dinner: Resort fine-dining tasting menu — 8-course chef's table experience with wine pairing; advance reservation required

day_by_day.notes: The helicopter sunset flight must be booked at least 3–5 days in advance through the concierge. Typically 20–30 minutes in duration, offering spectacular aerial views of the Benagil Cave, Ponta da Piedade, and Cabo de São Vicente.

day_by_day.morning: Private Ponta da Piedade Boat Tour — one of the Algarve's most iconic natural landmarks near Lagos. A private luxury motorboat tour weaves through the extraordinary golden rock arches, sea stacks, grottos, and emerald-green lagoons of Ponta da Piedade. Swim in secluded sea caves accessible only by boat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Lagos Old Town — a charming historic centre with whitewashed churches, Moorish-influenced architecture, and vibrant artisan shops. Visit the Igreja de Santo António (gilded baroque interior) and the Slave Market Museum. Browse high-end boutiques and local art galleries.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Lagos at one of the town's celebrated restaurants, followed by after-dinner drinks at a sophisticated wine bar in the historic centre.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch in Lagos — Restaurant recommendation: No Pátio (Lagos) — elegant courtyard restaurant specializing in fresh Algarve seafood with a refined wine list
meals.dinner: Restaurant recommendation: Casinha do Petisco (Lagos) — intimate, award-winning restaurant with creative Portuguese tasting menus; advance reservation essential

day_by_day.notes: Lagos is approximately 30–40 minutes from the resort by private transfer. The Ponta da Piedade boat tour is best in the morning when light is golden and seas are calmest. Wear non-slip shoes for the boat.

day_by_day.morning: Second Algarve Wine & Vineyard Experience — a deeper dive into Algarve wine culture. Visit a smaller boutique winery not covered on Day 4, such as Quinta da Tôr or Monte da Casteleja (organic wine estate). Enjoy a private blending workshop where you create your own personalized blend under the guidance of the resident winemaker — a unique luxury keepsake.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return via the scenic EN125 road stopping at a traditional local market or artisan ceramics studio (Porches Pottery is world-renowned for its hand-painted blue-and-white tiles and ceramics — a perfect luxury souvenir). Arrive back at the resort by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed resort evening — sunset cocktails on the terrace, followed by dinner at the resort's informal poolside restaurant for a more casual but still premium experience.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — full spread
meals.lunch: Winery estate lunch — a private farm-to-table meal prepared on-site using estate-grown vegetables, local meats, and paired with the winery's reserve collection
meals.dinner: Resort poolside restaurant — tapas-style sharing plates: pataniscas de bacalhau, gambas al ajillo, Iberian pork secreto, and a Douro red

day_by_day.notes: The personalized wine blending workshop results in a labeled bottle you can take home — arrange for the concierge to ship additional bottles to your home country if purchasing multiple cases. Porches Pottery is located along the main EN125 highway — easy stop en route.

day_by_day.morning: Private Sunrise Catamaran Cruise — depart from the marina at sunrise for a 3-hour luxury catamaran sail along the dramatic Algarve coastline. Glide past sea caves, golden cliffs, and hidden beaches only accessible from the water. Dolphin watching is highly likely in September. Champagne breakfast served on deck.
day_by_day.afternoon: Beach afternoon at the resort — rent a private beach cabana, enjoy watersports, or simply relax with a good book. Optional: book a 60-minute facial at the resort spa to refresh after days of sun exposure.
day_by_day.evening: Private chef dinner in your suite or on your private terrace — the resort can arrange for a personal chef to prepare a bespoke multi-course dinner tailored to your preferences, with a sommelier-selected wine pairing.

meals.breakfast: Champagne breakfast on the catamaran — smoked salmon blinis, fresh fruit, pastries, and Moët & Chandon
meals.lunch: Light resort poolside lunch — prawn cocktail, Caesar salad, and fresh coconut water
meals.dinner: In-suite private chef dinner — 5-course bespoke menu: amuse-bouche, lobster bisque, pan-seared turbot, aged Alentejo beef tenderloin, and a chocolate and almond fondant with Moscatel de Setúbal dessert wine

day_by_day.notes: Sunrise catamaran departures are typically around 07:00–07:30. Confirm exact timing with the charter company the evening before. September seas are generally calm with excellent visibility for dolphin spotting.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Tavira — one of the most elegant and authentically preserved towns in the Algarve. Explore the Roman bridge, the hilltop castle ruins, and the stunning collection of baroque churches. Stroll through the charming riverside market. Tavira is known as the 'Venice of the Algarve' for its network of waterways and bridges.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a traditional flat-bottomed boat (quatro águas ferry) to Ilha de Tavira — a stunning barrier island with miles of pristine, uncrowded beaches. Spend the afternoon on the beach before returning to the mainland by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Tavira before returning to the resort, celebrating the penultimate full day with a memorable meal in this historic town.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — full à la carte
meals.lunch: Lunch in Tavira — Restaurant recommendation: Patio de Tavira — elegant courtyard restaurant in a historic mansion serving refined Algarvian cuisine with exceptional fresh fish
meals.dinner: Restaurant recommendation: Aquasul (Tavira) — sophisticated riverside setting, celebrated for innovative seafood dishes and an outstanding Portuguese wine list; advance reservation recommended

day_by_day.notes: Tavira is approximately 1 hour from the resort by private transfer. The town is best explored on foot — wear comfortable shoes for the cobblestone streets. The Ilha de Tavira ferry runs regularly throughout the day.

day_by_day.morning: Final beach morning — a leisurely last full day at the resort. Enjoy a long breakfast, then head to the private beach for a final swim in the Atlantic. Paddleboard session or a last snorkel in the clear September waters. Alternatively, take a peaceful morning walk along the coastal path to a nearby viewpoint.
day_by_day.afternoon: Luxury spa afternoon — indulge in a signature 2-hour resort spa journey: body scrub, hydrotherapy circuit, and a relaxing hot stone massage. Followed by afternoon tea on the terrace with local almond cakes, pastéis de nata, and a glass of Moscatel.
day_by_day.evening: Grand farewell dinner — reserve the resort's finest table at the signature restaurant for a celebratory last dinner. Request the sommelier to curate a special wine journey through Portugal's finest regions (Douro, Alentejo, Dão) to complement a luxurious tasting menu. Toast to an unforgettable Algarve experience.

meals.breakfast: Champagne Sunday-style brunch at the resort — live stations, oysters, smoked fish, artisan pastries, and freshly squeezed juices
meals.lunch: Light beach club lunch — grilled sardines on toast, tomato salad, and a glass of chilled Alvarinho
meals.dinner: Resort signature farewell dinner — 7-course tasting menu with full Portuguese wine pairing; includes a complimentary glass of 20-year Tawny Port with dessert, arranged by the concierge as a farewell gesture

day_by_day.notes: Request the resort concierge to arrange a private transfer to Faro Airport for the following day. Confirm departure time and allow at least 2.5 hours before any flight for check-in. Pack any fragile wine or ceramics purchases carefully.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning — enjoy a last breakfast at the resort overlooking the Atlantic. Take a final walk on the beach, breathe in the sea air, and savour the last moments of the Algarve. Check out at the resort's convenience (late checkout can often be arranged for luxury guests — confirm with concierge).
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer departs for Faro Airport. Depending on flight time, a brief stop in Faro for last-minute shopping (local almonds, tinned fish, wine, and ceramics make excellent luxury gifts) can be arranged en route.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Faro Airport. The resort concierge will have arranged all luggage assistance and airport meet-and-greet services for a seamless end to your premium Algarve journey.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — full à la carte, savour every last bite of fresh pastéis de nata and Portuguese coffee
meals.lunch: Light airport lunch or lounge dining at Faro Airport (TAP Air Portugal Lounge or equivalent premium lounge available for business/first class passengers)
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Arrange late checkout (12:00–14:00) with the resort in advance to maximize your final morning. Faro Airport is approximately 45–60 minutes from most central Algarve locations. Duty-free at Faro Airport stocks excellent Portuguese wines, ginjinha, and Pastéis de Belém for gifts.
